Let \(\theta\in[0,1]\) be the de Finetti mixing parameter. Then

\[
\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_k=1)=\int_0^1 \theta^k\,d\mu(\theta),
\]

so the conditions are

\[
\int 1\,d\mu=1,\qquad \int\theta\,d\mu=\frac12,\qquad
\int\theta^2\,d\mu=\frac13,\qquad
\int\theta^3\,d\mu=\frac14.
\]

Also

\[
\mathbb P(X_7=1\mid X_1+\cdots+X_6=2)
=
\frac{\int \theta^3(1-\theta)^4\,d\mu}
{\int \theta^2(1-\theta)^4\,d\mu}.
\]

The extremal moment problem reduces to a measure supported at two interior atoms \(a<c\) and the endpoint \(1\). The moment equations give

\[
c=\frac{1-2a}{2-6a}.
\]

For such a measure the ratio is

\[
R(a)=
\frac{
4374-61236a+306180a^2-472392a^3-1207224a^4+5983632a^5-9552816a^6+6928416a^7-1889568a^8
}{
4374-65610a+428652a^2-1583388a^3+3551688a^4-4776408a^5+3464208a^6-944784a^7
}.
\]

The maximizing \(a\in(0,1/2)\) is the relevant root of

\[
\begin{aligned}
0={}&1-52a+870a^2-7456a^3+38536a^4-129984a^5+299808a^6\\
&-489216a^7+579264a^8-498240a^9+294624a^{10}-103680a^{11}+15552a^{12}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Eliminating \(a\) between this equation and \(T=R(a)\), and taking the irreducible factor containing the maximizing value \(E\approx0.508704693012965\), gives

\[
\boxed{
P(T)=1152T^6-8640T^5+21755T^4-66392T^3+97280T^2-55680T+10704
}.
\]

This polynomial is primitive, has positive leading coefficient, and is irreducible over \(\mathbb Z\) since its reduction modulo \(5\) is irreducible.
